strengths: Addresses a practical and under-explored problem: efficient initialization of variable-sized diffusion models without pre-trained models at each scale
Extends learngene framework to enable both size and task-specific model initialization, moving beyond prior size-only adaptation methods
Comprehensive baseline comparisons across multiple model sizes (L4-L12) and diverse downstream tasks (CelebA, LSUN-Bedroom, LSUN-Church)
Strong empirical results: 9.04 FID improvement (L6), 3× convergence speedup with 18% of parameters, 5× storage reduction for multiple models
Clear methodology with intuitive factorization framework (shared U,V for learngenes; layer-specific Σ for size/task adaptation)
Reproducible: provides hyperparameters, learning rates, batch sizes, and evaluation metrics
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: SVD-based decomposition for diffusion models exists (KIND, SVDiff); sharing U,V across layers is incremental; auxiliary model approach borrowed from TLEG

Critical experimental gaps: (1) KIND is absent from Table 1 despite being the most related work using SVD for diffusion models; (2) Only 10K downstream training steps evaluated—insufficient for conclusive initialization quality assessment (typical diffusion training is 50K+ steps); (3) Only DiT-B tested, no generalization to other architectures

Methodological clarity issues: Exact optimization procedure for enforcing constraint in Eq. (4) lacks detail; parameter sharing interval r=10 appears arbitrary without ablation; 'small amount of data' for downstream optimization is unspecified
No statistical rigor: n=5 runs with no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; unclear if improvements are statistically meaningful

Missing ablations and justifications: No comparison of shared vs. independent U,V decomposition; no validation that U,V capture size-agnostic knowledge; no justification for claiming 'first' to integrate size and task considerations

Confounded comparisons: Different baselines transfer different parameter counts (0-45.2M); FINE's 23.9M makes isolation of decomposition benefits difficult; insufficient analysis of parameter efficiency vs. method effectiveness
Lack of theoretical foundation: No explanation for why this factorization separates size-agnostic from size-specific knowledge; missing analysis of when size-agnostic knowledge exists
Limited experimental scope: All experiments at 256×256 resolution only; classifier-free guidance scale of 1.0 unusually low (typical 7.5); generalization beyond image generation unexplored

strengths: Addresses a practical problem: initializing diffusion models of varying sizes when pre-trained models of those sizes are unavailable
Clear presentation with informative figures (Figure 2) and well-motivated introduction
Extensive experiments across multiple model depths (L4-L12) and downstream datasets (ImageNet, CelebA, LSUN-Bedroom/Church)
First learngene method to incorporate task-specific initialization alongside size adaptation, going beyond prior size-only approaches
Consistent empirical improvements in FID/sFID scores with reduced parameter transfer (~23.9M parameters)
Multiple evaluation metrics (FID, sFID, IS) and comprehensive comparison against diverse baselines
weaknesses: Incremental novelty: core contribution (shared U,V in SVD decomposition) is a straightforward extension of KIND and SVDiff without sufficient theoretical justification for why weight sharing improves performance

Misleading efficiency claims: '3× speedup' and '3N× training steps savings' ignore the 30K-step auxiliary model cost. Fair accounting shows FINE uses 40K total steps vs. 30K for direct pre-training, contradicting efficiency narrative

Critical technical ambiguity on size adaptation: unclear how U,V dimensions (m₁, m₂) adapt when initializing models with different widths; no explanation of dimension matching mechanism in paper or figures

Unsubstantiated 'size-agnostic' knowledge claims: lacks theoretical justification and empirical validation; no ablation comparing shared vs. independent U,V; contradiction that Σ is 'randomly initialized' across sizes

Severely limited evaluation scope: only depth variation (L4-L12) tested; no width variation experiments; single patch size (p=2) and resolution (256×256); claims of 'variable-sized' models not validated

Missing critical ablations: no ablation on weight sharing mechanism; no analysis of auxiliary model contribution; no sensitivity studies on rank r or sharing interval s; no degradation analysis as model size deviates from auxiliary model
Unclear technical mechanism: constraint in Eq.(4) and extraction of learned U,V to downstream models poorly explained; parameter sharing in Σ (interval s=10) mentioned but never justified or ablated
Weak theoretical grounding: why auxiliary model training with sharing constraints is superior to direct decomposition lacks justification; borrowed from TLEG without clear adaptation rationale
Unfair baseline comparisons: some baselines (Heur-LG, Auto-LG) show surprisingly poor performance relative to simple Mimetic initialization—raises questions about proper implementation

Task-specific adaptation mechanism underdeveloped: claims training only Σ on small data is superior but provides no comparison to standard fine-tuning or LoRA-style adaptation; claims of 'few hundred steps' lack concrete numbers
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability stated; hyperparameter choices (r, s) lack justification; auxiliary model architecture sparse; n=5 runs without error bars or significance testing
Storage savings of '5×' (claimed in abstract) never explained or validated in paper body; wall-clock time comparisons missing despite computational cost claims

strengths: Addresses a practical and well-motivated problem of initializing variable-sized diffusion models when pre-trained variants are unavailable
Comprehensive evaluation against multiple baseline categories (direct initialization, conventional knowledge transfer, learngene-based methods) spanning 7 competing approaches
Consistent and meaningful performance improvements across variable depths (L4-L12) with up to 9.04 FID reduction and demonstrates 3× faster convergence in initialization speed
First learngene framework to jointly handle both model size and task-specific initialization requirements, extending beyond prior work limited to depth variation
Tests on diverse downstream datasets (ImageNet-1K, CelebA-HQ, LSUN-Bedroom, LSUN-Church) demonstrating broad applicability and task adaptability
Clear presentation with well-designed figures (especially Figure 2) effectively communicating the two-stage factorization and inheritance pipeline
Demonstrates parameter efficiency: achieving comparable results with only 23.9M parameters transferred vs. 45.3M for competing methods
weaknesses: Weak theoretical justification for core assumption: Why weight matrices across layers share singular vectors U and V is not principled. These encode information at different depths, making identical sharing counterintuitive and unjustified

Missing empirical evidence that shared U, V capture 'size-agnostic' knowledge: No analysis of singular value distributions, condition numbers, or interpretability studies to validate this central claim

Narrow experimental scope limits generalizability: (1) Single architecture (DiT-B only); unclear if generalizes to U-Net diffusion or other variants. (2) Depth variation only; no width experiments despite 'variable-sized models' claim. (3) Fixed 256×256 resolution; no evaluation at higher resolutions

Critical ablation studies missing: No ablation on weight sharing enforcement (shared vs. unshared U, V), parameter sharing interval sensitivity (why r=10?), downstream data requirements for Σ optimization, or auxiliary model training necessity

Auxiliary model mechanism (Eq. 4) under-explained and not ablated: How constraining with shared U, V produces good shared components lacks justification; no comparison to direct unconstrained optimization of U, Σ, V

Speedup claims partially misleading: 30K factorization cost is required regardless; actual speedup only appears when amortizing across N≥3 models, which is not realistic for single practitioners. Fair comparison should show total computational cost per model deployed
Lack of statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing reported despite n=5 runs per method; impossible to assess if improvements are significant vs. noise
No interpretability analysis: Missing visualization/analysis of learned U, V (singular values, patterns), what Σ learns across layers/tasks, or investigation of failure cases
Limited downstream task diversity and analysis: Only 3 downstream datasets; no investigation of why domain gap affects adaptation (e.g., why CelebA gains 3.61 FID vs. Church 2.93 FID)
Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; missing hyperparameter selection rationales (rank r, sharing interval s=10), auxiliary model initialization details, and sensitivity analyses

strengths: Addresses practical problem of variable-size diffusion model initialization with elegant factorization approach
Comprehensive experimental validation across 10 model sizes and 6 downstream datasets with consistent improvements (FID ↓4.89, IS ↑2.11)
3n× training speedup for initializing n models demonstrates significant practical efficiency gains
First comprehensive learngene-based initialization benchmark for diffusion models, providing useful community resource
Clear methodology and presentation; Figure 2 effectively illustrates the two-stage framework
Strong convergence behavior with FINE-initialized models reaching comparable FID ~200K steps earlier than scratch training
Extends to classification tasks (DeiT) demonstrating some architectural generality beyond diffusion models
Reasonable ablation studies examining factorization benefits (Table 4), initialization strategies (Table 5), and cross-scale structure (Figure 5)
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification: No explanation for why optimal singular vectors U* and V* should be shared across functionally different layer types (attention, feed-forward, adaLN); lacks convergence analysis for constrained optimization in Eq. (8)

Incremental novelty: Core contribution of adding cross-layer sharing to SVD-based decomposition is somewhat incremental over SVDiff and concurrent works (KIND, WAVE); insufficient differentiation from WAVE's constraint-based approach

Critical experimental gaps: Missing direct comparisons with SVDiff and KIND despite their high relevance; no statistical significance testing, error bars, or multiple runs reported; single-run results limit reliability

Severely limited architectural scope: Experiments almost exclusively on DiT; DeiT extension is minimal; no evaluation on standard UNet-based diffusion models (SD, etc.), limiting generalization claims

Underspecified design choices: Factorization rank r selection process not explained (Table 7 shows values without justification); why freeze U* and V* during initialization lacks justification; random initialization method for U, V in Algorithm 1 unspecified

Insufficient analysis of computational overhead: Pre-training cost (300K steps) not compared in GPU hours/memory; constraint optimization in Eq. (8) complexity not quantified; W reconstruction at every iteration (Algorithm 1, line 6) efficiency not analyzed
Modest downstream generalization: Table 2 shows marginal improvements on out-of-distribution datasets (e.g., Pokemon 0.011 FDD); unclear how domain-transferable learngenes truly are

Missing critical ablations: No sensitivity analysis for rank r; no failure case analysis; no ablation on joint vs. alternating optimization for U, V, S; unclear why post-hoc linear structure in Σ (Figure 5) emerges
Notation and presentation issues: Equation 7 notation θ = USV^T non-standard and confusing since U, V, S are sets; 'reverse SVD' terminology vague; biological metaphor adds little technical value
Reproducibility concerns: No code availability mentioned; hyperparameter selection (1e-4 LR) appears dataset-independent without sensitivity analysis; VAE version specificity may affect comparability

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: initializing variable-sized diffusion models efficiently without maintaining model zoo
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three baseline categories, six downstream datasets, and both generative/classification tasks
Consistent empirical improvements in FID/sFID/IS metrics across model depths with demonstrated 3n× training speedup
Solid ablation studies examining factorization components and initialization strategies (Tables 4-5)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of framework architecture
Practical utility: accelerates convergence and demonstrates reasonable transfer across diverse downstream domains
weaknesses: Limited novelty over existing SVD-based methods (KIND, SVDiff): primarily adds layer-specific Σ^(l) while sharing U,V—incremental rather than fundamental innovation

Insufficient theoretical justification: 'size-agnostic knowledge' is assumed but not rigorously defined; why should shared singular vectors work across depths L4-L12 for diffusion models differs from ViTs
Experimental scope issues: downstream datasets (CelebA, LSUN) are visually similar to ImageNet; truly out-of-distribution evaluation lacking (medical/artistic domains are small <3.7K images)

Unfair baseline comparisons: TLEG and other learngene methods weren't designed for diffusion; adapting them is non-trivial, making FINE comparison venue questionable rather than fundamental superiority
Figure 3c shows FINE-initialized DiT-L still significantly lags directly pre-trained models at 800K steps, contradicting claims about initialization quality translating to full training
Overclaimed 'first comprehensive benchmark': adapting existing learngene methods to diffusion doesn't constitute novel benchmarking; setting (10 depths) is straightforward
Critical missing ablations: no sensitivity analysis for rank r, no ablation on layer-specific vs. shared components for U,V, no comparison with simply fine-tuning pre-trained models

Algorithm 1 and Eq. (6) lack clarity: how 'reverse factorization' differs algorithmically from standard SVD-regularized training is vague; optimization procedure for jointly updating shared U,V and layer-specific Σ unexplained
Limited architectural generality: only Diffusion Transformers evaluated; generalization to U-Net/other diffusion architectures unclear; DeiT classification task feels disconnected
No statistical significance testing; improvements sometimes marginal and within potential noise (Table 1: many <3 FID points)
Reproducibility concerns: 300K pre-training steps substantial, no code release mentioned, hyperparameter choices (r=100/148, lr=1e-4) lack justification

Method design choices unexplained: why freeze U,V during downstream initialization rather than fine-tune? Why does 35% parameter transfer (Table 2) outperform full FT, suggesting redundancy not size-agnosticity?
Insufficient positioning vs. WAVE [11] (constraint-based pre-training, CVPR'25): no quantitative comparison despite similar concurrent work
Figure 5 visualization of Σ linearity is interesting but barely analyzed—lacks interpretation of what explains learned structure
No discussion of failure modes, limitations, or scenarios where FINE underperforms; no analysis of learned representations in U,V across weight matrix types

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem with clear real-world deployment scenario for variable-sized diffusion models
First comprehensive benchmark for evaluating learngene-based initialization in image generation - valuable community contribution

Comprehensive experimental validation: multiple model sizes (DiT-B/L L4-L12), diverse downstream datasets (6 datasets), extensive baselines (3 categories), multiple metrics, consistent improvements up to 4.89 FID reduction
Sound technical approach with cross-layer weight sharing that captures size-agnostic knowledge through joint pre-training of U, V, Σ
Practical efficiency gains with ~3× speedup when initializing multiple models across different sizes
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating advantages over layer-wise SVD (Table 4) and benefits of trainable Σ initialization (Table 5)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations explaining the two-stage framework and learned structure (Figure 5)
Extension to classification tasks (DeiT) demonstrates some architectural generality beyond diffusion models
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core factorization concept builds incrementally on existing work (KIND, SVDiff, WAVE) with main contribution being application to diffusion models with cross-layer sharing

Insufficient theoretical justification: why should U and V be truly size-agnostic beyond empirical observation of stacked blocks? No formal analysis of why joint pre-training outperforms post-hoc SVD extraction or convergence guarantees

Incomplete cost-benefit analysis: 300K pre-training steps required matches direct pre-training costs; speedup primarily from amortization across multiple models, not method efficiency itself. Single-model deployment may not benefit

Missing critical implementation details: rank r selection process unclear, no sensitivity analysis on r choices despite direct impact on reusability and memory savings; unclear what 'sigma share B: 100 | L: 148' means
Discrepancy between claims and results: Section 3.3 claims 'light retraining' but Table 1 shows 100K step training; Figure 3b mentions '0.3K vs 300K' conflicting with Table 1 methodology
Mixed domain transfer performance: in-distribution improvements modest (0.28-2.60 FID), out-of-distribution gains marginal (0.006-0.018 FDD), contradicting claims of 'task-agnostic versatility'

Fairness concerns in comparisons: FINE requires substantial 300K pre-training overhead not required by all baselines; paper lacks discussion of when this overhead is justified versus simpler alternatives
Limited architectural scope: primarily evaluated on DiTs with only tangential DeiT extension; generalization to CNNs and other architectures unclear despite broad claims about diffusion models
No statistical rigor: missing error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; benchmark paper needs variance characterization

Reproducibility gaps: code release not mentioned, vague initialization details ('randomly initialized' Σ without distribution specification), Algorithm 1 lacks precision on gradient computation details
